description: Sample knowledge base for an internal developer-tools support group. Replace every entry with your own. The bot sends `answer` verbatim, so write it exactly the way you want it to appear in the chat.

triggers: can't reach internal sites from home
error_strings: The VPN connection failed due to unsuccessful domain name resolution
entries.answer:
VPN checklist:
1. Quit the VPN client completely (not just disconnect) and reopen it.
2. Make sure you are on the *Corp-Remote* profile, not *Corp-Guest*.
3. If it still fails, toggle Wi-Fi off and on. Hotel and cafe networks often block UDP 443; switch to your phone's hotspot to confirm.

Still stuck after that? Open a ticket with the exact error text and the time it happened.

triggers: have to sign in again and again
sso keeps asking me to log in
error_strings: The refresh token has expired due to inactivity
entries.answer:
This is expected: the company's Conditional Access policy limits developer-tool sessions to 4 hours.

The fix is to let the CLI reuse your browser session instead of an isolated profile:
```
devtool config set browser.profile default
```
After that, a sign-in lasts as long as your normal browser login does. If you still get AADSTS70043, delete the folder `~/.devtool/chrome-profile` and sign in once more.

triggers: how do I install the cli on windows
entries.answer:
Windows install, three steps:
1. Open the *Software Center* and install **DevTool CLI**. Do not download it from the internet; the internal build carries the proxy settings you need.
2. Open a new terminal and run `devtool setup`. It will open the browser for sign-in.
3. Run `devtool doctor`. Everything should be green.

Mac and Linux: `brew install acme/tap/devtool`, then the same two commands.

triggers: can't reach the api from the office network
entries.answer:
A 403 from the office network means the destination is not on the egress allowlist yet. Nothing is wrong with your setup.

Send the exact hostname (for example `api.example.com`) to the network team in #net-access with a one-line business reason. Approval usually takes one working day.

Tip: `devtool doctor --network` prints every host the tool needs, so you can request them all at once.

triggers: git push asks for a password
my personal access token stopped working
entries.answer:
Personal access tokens expire after 90 days, and Git keeps trying the old one.

1. Create a new token in *User settings > Personal access tokens* with the **Code (read & write)** scope.
2. Remove the stale one from your credential store:
   - Windows: Control Panel > Credential Manager > Windows Credentials > remove the `git:https://...` entry.
   - Mac: Keychain Access > search the host > delete.
3. Run `git pull` once; paste the new token when asked.

triggers: cannot connect to the docker daemon
error_strings: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock
error during connect: this error may indicate that the docker daemon is not running
entries.answer:
The Docker daemon is not running.

- Mac/Windows: start **Docker Desktop** from the applications menu and wait for the whale icon to stop animating.
- Linux: `sudo systemctl start docker`, then `sudo usermod -aG docker $USER` and log out and back in so you can run it without sudo.

If Docker Desktop refuses to start on Windows, make sure WSL 2 is enabled: `wsl --status`.

triggers: who can add me to the tool
I don't have permission to use devtool
error_strings: You are not a member of an authorized group
entries.answer:
Access is granted through the AD group **DevTool-Users**.

Ask your manager to approve you in the *Access Portal* (search for "DevTool"). Sync to the tool takes up to 30 minutes after approval; sign out and back in once to pick it up.

triggers: am I on the current version
entries.answer:
Current release: **1.4.2** (2026-09-01).

Check yours with `devtool --version` and update with `devtool update`. Release notes are posted in #devtool-announcements every Monday.
